title: Tenali Rama and the Thieves
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Tenali Rama
cast.description: Witty court jester-poet, mischievous adult man

cast.name: Tenali's wife
cast.description: Sharp, amused wife who plays along

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Telugu tradition. It is one of the tales of Tenali Ramakrishna, the jester-poet of the court of Vijayanagara. It is called... Tenali Rama and the Thieves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tenali Ramakrishna was famous for turning trouble into a joke, and a joke into a lesson.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One summer the rains failed. The wells sank low, and Tenali's garden withered. Drawing enough water to save it would take him all night... [amused] and he was not fond of hard work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, coming home, he noticed shadows crouched behind the bushes. Thieves, he thought, waiting for the lamps to go out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He went inside, stood right by the window, and spoke in a loud, worried voice.

lines.speaker: tenali
lines.text: [loudly, theatrical] Wife! There are thieves about this season. Our jewels and silver are not safe. Let us put them in the trunk and drop it into the well. No one will think to look there!

lines.speaker: wife
lines.text: [playing along, loudly] What a clever idea! Quickly, before anyone sees!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Together they filled the old trunk with stones, carried it out with great show, and heaved it into the well... with a mighty splash. Then they blew out the lamp.

lines.speaker: thief
lines.text: [whispering, greedy] The trunk's at the bottom. Draw out the water. All of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] Bucket after bucket, they hauled up water and poured it on the ground, which drank it gratefully, all through the night.

lines.speaker: tenali
lines.text: [whispers, giggling] Wife... I think they're watering the chillies now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At dawn, sore and soaked, the thieves finally pulled up the trunk, and found it full of stones.

lines.speaker: tenali
lines.text: [cheerfully, stretching] Thank you, friends! Come back next week... the mango trees are thirsty too!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [laughs] The thieves ran. And his garden was the greenest in the city that summer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Tenali's tales remind us that a quick mind can turn even a threat into help. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
